findings.title: Pagination creates a phantom page when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit
findings.body: `totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, so a group with exactly 50 members and the default limit reports two pages. The Next control is enabled, requests offset 50, and renders an empty member page. The same issue occurs after deleting the sole member on a final partial page when the remaining count becomes an exact multiple. Use a ceiling division (and clamp offsets after a reload) so only pages containing members are reachable.

findings.title: Membership pagination accepts an unbounded client-controlled limit
findings.body: The public members endpoint passes `params[:limit].to_i` directly to ActiveRecord without enforcing a positive maximum. Any user allowed to view a group can request an arbitrarily large limit, causing the server to load and serialize the entire membership in one response; zero or negative values can also produce database-specific invalid/unbounded query behavior. Clamp `limit` to a reasonable maximum and normalize invalid offsets/limits before querying.

findings.title: Automatic-group removal test exercises the wrong HTTP verb
findings.body: The remove-member route added by this change is DELETE `/admin/groups/:group_id/members`, and the client sends DELETE, but this automatic-group test invokes the controller action with PUT. Direct controller action tests do not validate route/verb wiring, so this does not cover the actual request used in production. Change it to DELETE and preferably add a route/request-level assertion for the members endpoint.
